## Closing state — the code work landed; the attestation is still outstanding

The Terraform change merged as **`213341e3e58faf021f51ddd7db0285f57d95f2b9`** ("Grant Titan
embedding ARN to Bedrock policy", `rebar-ticket: f10f-c24a-3cfa-449e`,
`Change-Id: I434df308687c03cbe456693954ba3363ed1e9cec`). Verified on `origin/main`:

- `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:20` carries
  `arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0`
- both Claude ARNs remain at `:18-19`
- the sid at `:12` is now `InvokeScopedBedrockModels` — no Anthropic-only assertion
- the header comment at `:5` reads "the Claude models it converses with and the Titan model
  it embeds"

14 of 15 acceptance criteria are checked. The 15th is `[non-codebase]` and is exempt from
the close gate: `ensure_ac_boxes_checked` (`src/rebar/_commands/txn.py`) filters unchecked
lines through `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` and raises only on the remainder. That exemption
is the ADR-0101 behaviour working as designed, not a bypass — no `--force` is involved.

**What is genuinely still open, and it is not a code question.** Nobody has applied this
Terraform to the deployment or made a real Titan call from the Gerrit instance role. The
ticket's own analysis explains why nothing cheaper settles it: no Gerrit gate applies this
Terraform (`terraform-drift.yml` fires on `pull_request`, `schedule` and
`workflow_dispatch`, none of which a Gerrit change triggers, and its header disclaims the
Verified label), and the policy simulator cannot answer it because Converse authorizes
against `bedrock:InvokeModel` while the distinct `bedrock:Converse` action simulates as
denied.

So the open item is **authorization to apply a production IAM change**, not capability and
not tooling. That decision belongs to an operator, which is precisely what the tagged
criterion records.

**This blocks nothing.** The ticket states it directly: "It is not a feature blocker: the
lexical tier the sibling index story builds requires no model provider at all, so
similar-ticket retrieval works without this change everywhere, including here." An
unapplied grant degrades the embedding tier to lexical retrieval; it does not break it.

Closing on that basis. The tagged criterion stays unchecked as the durable record that the
attestation is owed.
